boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named downtown New London destinations along documented corridors near the Academy.

cards.title: Hygienic Art on Bank Street
cards.subtitle: Bank Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Walk Bank Street to 79–83 and check the gallery’s current exhibition or Art Park program before planning a visit.
cards.short_summary: A documented gallery and art-park stop on the downtown Bank Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Connecticut’s tourism office lists Hygienic Art Galleries & Art Park at 79–83 Bank Street and describes it as a venue for emerging and established artists.
cards.access_notes: The source lists gallery hours; confirm the current exhibition and access details directly before going.

cards.title: Custom House on Bank Street
cards.subtitle: Bank Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Use Bank Street to reach 150 Bank Street and focus your visit on the museum’s New London waterfront collections.
cards.short_summary: A maritime-history destination on the same downtown corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies the New London Customhouse at 150 Bank Street as a National Register site managed by the New London Maritime Society.
cards.access_notes: Museum admission and visiting arrangements may apply; check the operator’s current information.

cards.title: Garde on State Street
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Head to 325 State Street and review the current calendar for performances, films, or education programs.
cards.short_summary: A named performing-arts venue on State Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Garde Arts Center’s official site gives its address as 325 State Street, New London.
cards.access_notes: Ticketing and event availability vary; consult the center’s current schedule.

cards.entity_name: Timothy Green’s New London Summary Site
cards.title: Timothy Green’s State Street site
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Pause at 158 State Street and use the city’s historic-figures page to connect the building with early Connecticut newspapers.
cards.short_summary: A surviving 1771 State Street building tied to New London’s early press history.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of New London identifies 158 State Street as the site of Timothy Green’s New London Summary and says the 1771 building survived the burning of the city.
cards.access_notes: View from the public street; the source documents the historic site but does not state public interior access.

cards.title: Hotel Bristol on Bank Street
cards.subtitle: Bank Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Find the 90 Bank Street trail location and read the city’s Black Heritage Trail entry before or while you walk the block.
cards.short_summary: A Bank Street stop included in New London’s Black Heritage Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of New London’s Black Heritage Trail lists the Hotel Bristol at 90 Bank Street and documents its connection to a 1919 racial-violence incident.
cards.access_notes: This is a historic trail location; use public sidewalks and respect any private property.

cards.title: Shiloh on Garvin Street
cards.subtitle: Garvin Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Include 1 Garvin Street on a heritage walk and use the city’s trail entry for context on the congregation’s history.
cards.short_summary: New London’s oldest historically Black church, documented by the city trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of New London lists Shiloh Baptist Church at 1 Garvin Street and identifies it as the city’s oldest historically Black church.
cards.access_notes: Observe from public areas unless the church publicly invites visitors inside.

cards.title: Amistad Pier at Waterfront Park
cards.subtitle: Water Street waterfront corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Use the waterfront path to locate the Amistad Pier entrance and read the trail account of the schooner’s 1839 arrival.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront trail stop interpreting New London’s connection to La Amistad.
cards.evidence_claim: New London’s Black Heritage Trail identifies the Amistad Pier entrance at Waterfront Park and recounts that the schooner was towed into New London Harbor in 1839.
cards.access_notes: Use the public waterfront park entrance; the source does not list an admission charge.

cards.title: 38 Green Street’s civic-history stop
cards.subtitle: Green Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Add 38 Green Street to a self-guided heritage walk and use the city trail page for the site’s civic-history context.
cards.short_summary: A Green Street Black Heritage Trail location tied to community organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: The city’s Black Heritage Trail says 38 Green Street housed the New England Peoples Finance Corporation and United Negro Welfare Council in the late 1920s.
cards.access_notes: View from the public right-of-way and respect the property’s current use.

cards.title: Antone DeSant’s Bank Street site
cards.subtitle: Bank Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Locate 745 Bank Street and read the city’s entry on DeSant and the Cape Verdean whalers who came to New England.
cards.short_summary: A named Bank Street site on the Black Heritage Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of New London’s Black Heritage Trail lists the Antone DeSant site at 745 Bank Street and describes DeSant’s arrival as part of a wave of Cabo Verdeans on whaling vessels.
cards.access_notes: This is a historic-location stop; view it from public areas unless access is explicitly offered.

cards.title: Spark on Union Street
cards.subtitle: Union Street corridor, downtown New London
cards.notes: Walk to 7 Union Street and check Spark Maker Space’s current public program or workshop details before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A named creative-workspace destination on Union Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of New London’s Explore New London site states that Spark Maker Space moved to 7 Union Street in downtown New London.
cards.source_title: New London Tales – Explore New London
cards.access_notes: Workshop access and costs vary by program; verify current visitor information with Spark Maker Space.
